text:
A: Hello! Kem cho, bhai? Can you hear me?
B: Ha, yeah, I can hear you. Erm, majama. That's about as far as my Gujarati goes, to be honest.
A: Ha! London Gujarati, I know. Hitesh, Peterborough. I said to Gurpreet before, last call, finished, but no, they give me one more. Good, I like talking.
B: Nilesh. Kingsbury. Nice to meet you. I saw your photo, you've got the Ganesh calendar.
A: Free one, from the grocery shop! You also have Ganesh, the little shrine. And same hoodie, look, navy. We're twins, mate.
B: Ha, yeah, we are a bit. Erm, so what do you do?
A: Chilled food factory, flow-wrap machine. Part-time, but I do delivery also, moped, evenings. With both, I'm making more than full-time guys, easy.
B: Oh, right. That's good. I'm in chilled food as well, Park Royal. Tray-sealer, full-time, rotating shifts.
A: Everybody in this study is chilled food! Gurpreet also, tray-sealer. They put all the factory guys together. How long you're there?
B: Eleven years now. I train the new starters on the sealer, sort of thing. They're talking about team leader, maybe.
A: Team leader, that's good, take it, mate. More money. Me, they should make me team leader, I know every shortcut, but supervisor doesn't like me. Two warnings, for lateness. Bus is always late, what can I do?
B: Yeah, the North Circular's the same for me. Nightmare most mornings.
A: You drive forklift?
B: Yeah, I've got the counterbalance licence. Work put me through it.
A: Everybody has licence except me! Gurpreet also. I'm driving it, no licence. Okay, okay, I will book it. Three people told me today.
B: Honestly, it's only a few days. Worth it.
A: You watch IPL?
B: Yeah, with my dad, mostly. He gets really into it. Erm, he's not been so well lately, so it's sort of our thing now, you know, sitting together.
A: That's nice. That's very nice. My father is in Gujarat, he's also not well. I can't sit with him, I only argue on WhatsApp about cricket. Your dad is close?
B: Ten minutes, in Kenton. My mum keeps sending dinner round, so I can't complain.
A: Lucky man. Me, my brother is in Leicester, he has shop, doing very well, he can go to India whenever. I'm, you know, factory. Anyway. Sorry, sorry, what was I saying?
B: Erm, your dad, but it's fine. Do you get back much?
A: Every two, three years. Should be more. You go India?
B: Once, 2019, cousin's wedding. Hot, loud, lovely. My parents came from Kenya, actually, so I'd like to take the kids there one day, see where my dad grew up.
A: Kenya Gujarati! So that's why your Gujarati is broken, ha. Sorry, sorry, joking.
B: No, it's true. My mum says the same thing every week.
A: Your kids speak?
B: Not really. That's sort of what bothers me, you know. I can't teach them what I haven't got.
A: Send them to Peterborough for summer, Komal will teach them in one week. My kids, Gujarati at home, all the time. Dev answers in English, cheeky boy, but he—
